full_judgment:
A.K.M. Fazlur Rahman, J: This Rule was issued at the instance of accused-petitioners (1) Hazi Aminul Islam and (2) Noor Islam on an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 3.3.2003 passed by the Additional Sessions Judge, Sirajganj in Criminal Revision No. 93 of 2002 allowing the revision and setting aside the order dated 5.10.2002 passed by the Magistrate 1st Class, Sirajganj in G.R. Case No. 366 of 1994 arising out of Rayganj Police Station Case No. 6 dated 19.10.1994 dismissing the naraji petition filed by the informant and discharging the accused persons, should not be quashed. 

 3. On the basis of that First Information Report Rayganj Police Station Case No. 6 dated 19.10.1994 under section 302/34 of the Penal Code was started against eight accused persons, namely (1) Selimuddin, (2) Atab Ali, (3) Mohammad Ali, (4) Joy Chand, (5) Kalu Bapari, (6) Ahmed Ali, (7) Abdul Quddus and (8) Mulluk Chand. After investigation of the case on 24.4.1997 police of CID submitted Charge sheet against five accused persons, including two First Information Report, namely accused Md. Selim and Atab Ali and Final Report against remaining six namely (1) Mohammad Ali, (2) Joy Chand, (3) Kalu Bapari, (4) Ahmed Ali, (5) Abdul Quddus and (6) Mulluk Chand. On 8.5.1997 the informant filed a naraji petition against that Police Report. The learned Magistrate by his order dated 10.7.1997 rejected the naraji petition and accepted the Charge sheet and the Final Report, and discharged six First Information Report named accused persons. Against that order the informant preferred Criminal Revision No. 47 of 1997 before the Sessions Judge, Sirajganj, which was rejected. Against that order the informant moved this Court on an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, which was registered as Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1227 of 1999 and obtained Rule. After hearing the Rule was made absolute by the order dated 3.7.2001 directing the Magistrate to dispose of the naraji petition complying with the provisions of sections 200, 202 and 203 of the Code of Criminal Procedure treating the naraji petition as a petition of complaint. But the learned Magistrate being misconceived without complying with the provisions of those sections of the Code as directed by this Court on 21.8.2001 ordered the Officer-in-Charge of Rayganj Police Station to submit Charge sheet against the six First Information Report named accused persons against whom earlier Final Report was submitted. Against that order accused Kalu Bapari moved this Court by filing another application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, which was registered as Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 2003 of 2002 and obtained Rule. The Rule was ultimately made absolute quashing the order of the Magistrate dated 21.8.2001 with a direction to the Magistrate to dispose of the naraji petition following the procedure provided in sections 200, 202 and 203 of the Code of Criminal Procedure as ordered by this Court earlier in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1227 of 1999. The learned Magistrate accordingly took up the matter. At that stage on 23.3.2002 the informant filed a new petition of complaint naming thirteen accused persons, of whom five were charge sheeted, six were First Information Report named accused persons against whom earlier Final Report was submitted and the present petitioners. The learned Magistrate leaving that fresh petition of complaint out of consideration as per direction of this Court treating the naraji petition dated 8.5.1997 as petition of complaint held judicial enquiry under section 202 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. During such enquiry the learned Magistrate recorded the statements of nine witnesses, including the complainant and on consideration of the same and other materials on record by the order dated 29.9.2002 suggested rejection of the naraji petition. Then the learned Magistrate by the order dated 5.10.2002 dismissed the naraji petition under section 203 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and sent the case to the Sessions Judge, Sirajganj for trial. Against that order of rejecting naraji petition the informant filed Criminal Revision No. 93 of 2002 under section 435/439A of the Code of Criminal Procedure before the Sessions Judge, Sirajganj, which was heard by the Additional Sessions Judge, Sirajganj, who by the order dated 3.3.2003 allowed the revision and set aside the order of the Magistrate dated 5.10.2002 rejecting the naraji petition and directed the learned Magistrate to take cognizance of the offence against all the thirteen accused persons named in the fresh petition of complaint filed on 23.3.2002. Against that order the petitioners moved this Court with the present application under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and obtained this Rule. 

 4. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners, supporting the Rule submits that the learned Additional Sessions Judge had no jurisdiction to direct the Magistrate to take cognizance of the offence against the accused persons and as such the impugned order is illegal and abuse of the process of the court, which should be quashed. He further submits that occurrence took place on 11.10.1994 and First Information Report was lodged on 19.10.1994, wherein the petitioners were not named as accused. In the naraji petition filed on 8.5.1997 also they were not named as accused. This Court in Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos. 1227 of 1999 and 2003 of 2002 directed the Magistrate to proceed in accordance with sections 200, 202 and 203 of the Penal Code treating the naraji petition dated 8.5.1997 as a petition of complaint. When the learned Magistrate was proceeding with the matter, on 23.3.2003 the informant filed a fresh petition of complaint, wherein for the first time the names of the petitioners with those of First Information Report named accused and charge sheeted accused were mentioned. He also submits that the learned Magistrate as per direction of this Court treating the naraji petition dated 8.5.1997 as a petition of complaint held judicial enquiry in accordance with the sections 200 and 202 of the Code, when he recorded the statements of nine witnesses. The learned Magistrate after proper consideration of those statements and other material on record rightly and legally rejected the naraji petition as no prima facie case was made out against the six accused who were left out of the charge sheet. There was no scope of filing fresh petition of complaint on 23.3.2002 naming the petitioners as accused as the naraji petition filed earlier was pending. This Court directed the Magistrate to proceed with the naraji petition dated 8.5.1997 in accordance with law treating the same as a petition of complaint. In that case the learned Magistrate had no jurisdiction to hold enquiry on the fresh petition of complaint filed on 23.3.2002. But the learned Additional Sessions Judge found fault with the Magistrate for not considering the fresh complaint and illegally directed the learned Magistrate to take cognizance against all the thirteen accused persons named in the fresh petition of complaint filed on 23.3.2003. His such order being abuse of the process of the Court should be quashed. 

 6. Mr. Muhammad Roushan Ali, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party No. 2, opposing the Rule submits that the learned Magistrate did not comply with the direction of this Court given in Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos. 1227 of 1999 and 2003 of 2002 and without complying the provisions of sections 200, 202 and 203 of the Code and without considering the statements of the complaint and his witnesses recorded by him at the time of judicial enquiry illegally rejected the naraji petition. Therefore, the learned Additional Sessions Judge rightly set aside such illegal order of the Magistrate and directed him to take cognizance of the offence against all the accused persons named in the fresh complaint filed on 23.3.2002. He further submits that it is not true that in the petition of complaint filed on 23.3.2002 for the first time the petitioners were made accused. Their names at first transpired from the list of the accused sent by accused Selimuddin from the jail, who earlier made a confessional statement recorded under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. According to Mr. Md. Roushan Ali there is no legal ground for quashing the impugned order of the learned Additional Sessions Judge and as such the Rule should be discharged. 

 7. We have perused the application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the First Information Report, the Charge sheet, the statement of witness Johura Khatun recorded under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the confession of accused Selimuddin, the Naraji petition filed on 8.5.1997, the Judgment and order passed by this Court in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 2003 of 2002, the Petition of Complaint filed on 23.3.2002, the orders of the Magistrate dated 29.9.2002, and 5.10.2002 and the impugned judgment and order of the learned Additional Sessions Judge, annexed therewith and considered the above submissions of the learned Advocates. 

 9. During investigation of the case First Information Report named accused Selimuddin made a confession recorded under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure implicating himself, co-accused Atab Ali, Roman, Rana and Karim in the killing of the deceased. Atab Ali was one of the First Information named accused. Roman, Rana and Karim were not named therein. Statement of Johura Khatun, mother-in-law of accused Atab Ali was recorded under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, who stated that on the night of occurrence her son-in-law Atab Ali, accused Selimuddin, deceased Rafiq and two unidentified others stayed in their house. At first, investigation of the case was taken up by police of Rayganj Police Station. Then Criminal Investigation Department took up investigation of the case. Lastly Nab Kumar Das, Assistant Superintendent of Police, C.I.D, Pabna Zone, concluding investigation of the case submitted Charge sheet on 24.4.1997 against five accused persons, namely Selimuddin and Atab Ali, the First Information Report named accused, Rana, Roman and Karim, not First Information Report named, but named in the confession of accused Selimuddin, and Final Report against the remaining six First Information Report named accused persons namely, Mohammad Ali, Joy Chand, Kalu Bapari, Ahmed Ali, Abdul Quddus and Kulluk Chand. Against that Final Report the informant filed naraji petition on 8.5.1997, which was rejected by the learned Magistrate on 10.7.1997. Against that order the informant filed Criminal Revision No. 47 of 1997 before the Sessions Judge, Sirajganj, which was rejected. Against that order the informant moved this Court filing an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, which was registered as Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1227 of 1999 and Rule was issued. Ultimately the Rule was made absolute directing the Magistrate to proceed with the naraji petition treating the same as a petition of complaint and complying the provisions of sections 200, 202 and 203 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. But the learned Magistrate without complying such direction of this Court asked the officer-in-charge of the Police Station to submit Charge sheet against the six accused persons against whom earlier Final Report was submitted. Against that order accused Kalu Bapari moved this Court by filing another application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and obtained Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 2003 of 2002, which was ultimately made absolute setting aside the order of the Magistrate directing the Officer-in-Charge of the Police Station to submit Charge sheet against the remaining six accused persons and directing the Magistrate to comply with the direction of this Court given in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1227 of 2001. 

 10. This Court in Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos. 1227 of 1999 and 2003 of 2002 directed the Magistrate to proceed with the naraji petition dated 8.5.1997 treating the same as a petition of complaint and complying with the provisions of the sections 200, 202 and 203 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. In that naraji petition the names of these two petitioners as accused were not mentioned. The First Information Report named eight accused persons therein. As per direction of this Court while the learned Magistrate was proceeding with the naraji petition dated 8.5.1997 treating the same as a petition of complaint, the informant on 23.3.2002 filed a fresh petition of the complaint naming thirteen accused persons, of whom eight were named in the First Information Report and naraji petition, three were Charge sheet named and two petitioners. More then eight years after the occurrence informant for the first time made the petitioners as the accused in the fresh petition of complaint. Accused Selimuddin in his confession did not implicate the petitioners. But one year after his confession he from the jail sent a list of the some people, who allegedly killed the deceased. In that list the names of the petitioners were included. Such list is of no legal value and is not a material for consideration for taking cognizance of the offence on the basis of the naraji petition. 

 13. It is well settled that neither the, Sessions Judge nor this Court is invested with any power to direct any Magistrate to take cognizance of an offence against any accused. In this regard the case Yusuf A. Hasan Vs. K.M. Rezaul Firdous reported in 48 DLR (AD) 53 may be referred. So in the instant case the learned Additional Sessions Judge acted beyond his jurisdiction directing the learned Magistrate to take cognizance of the offence against all the thirteen accused persons named in the fresh petition of complaint filed on 23.3.2002. The learned Additional Sessions Judge wrongly considered that petition of complaint and found fault with the learned Magistrate for non-consideration of the same. The learned Magistrate rightly left the petition of complaint out of consideration as it was not legally entertainable in presence of the naraji petition, which was treated as a petition of complaint. Thus the impugned order of the learned Additional Sessions Judge was not in accordance with law. As such the same being abuse of the process of the Court should be quashed. 

 14. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The impugned order dated 3.3.2003 passed by the Additional Sessions Judge, Sirajganj in Criminal Revision No. 93 of 2002 is hereby set aside. The Sessions Case No.195/2002 of the Court of Sessions Judge, Sirajganj arising out of G.R. Case No. 366 of 1994 corresponding to Rayganj P.S. Case No. 6 dated 19.10.1994 as against accused (1) Atab Ali, (2) Selimuddin, (3) Rana, (4) Roman and (5) Karim alias Abdul Karim will proceed according to law.
